extra.message: JWT signature verification disabled on /get/<cust_id> — Complete authentication bypass for the customer-retrieval endpoint; attacker forges any token to read customer PII and credit card numbers. [verified: insecure_verify calls jwt.decode(token, verify=False) and unconditionally returns True; it guards GET /get/<cust_id>, so any forged token bypasses auth (app.py:97,232).]

SQL injection in customer search — Read/exfiltrate the entire database including user password hashes and customer credit card numbers; potentially modify data via stacked logic. [verified: content['search'] is string-formatted into str_query and run via db.engine.execute with no parameterization; only guard is a forgeable JWT, so any authenticated/forged caller injects SQL (app.py:261).]

Insecure YAML deserialization (RCE) — Arbitrary code execution on the server by uploading a malicious YAML payload. [verified: yaml.load(y) uses PyYAML's default FullLoader/Loader on attacker-uploaded file at /yaml_hammer, permitting !!python/object payloads for RCE (app.py:329).]

Hardcoded weak JWT signing secret — Attackers forge valid JWTs for any user, bypassing authentication on all JWT-protected routes. [verified: SECRET_KEY_HMAC='secret' is hardcoded and used for both jwt.encode at login and verify_jwt, so attackers forge valid HS256 tokens (app.py:26).]

Plaintext admin password and plaintext credential comparison — Database compromise immediately yields usable admin credentials; no protection of stored secrets. [verified: Seeded admin stores password 'admin123' in plaintext and login does filter_by(username, password) comparing plaintext, so DB compromise yields usable creds (app.py:62,180).]

SSTI/reflected XSS via request.url in 404 handler — Remote code execution on the server via Jinja2 sandbox escape and/or reflected XSS in the victim browser. [verified: 404 handler does template = '...%s...' % request.url then render_template_string(template), making attacker-controlled URL Jinja2 source enabling SSTI/reflected XSS (app.py:114).]

IDOR/BOLA on customer retrieval endpoints — Cross-customer data access; full enumeration of all customer PII and credit card numbers. [verified: fetch_customer and get_customer return Customer.query.get(id) for any client-supplied id with no ownership/tenant check, enabling enumeration of all customers (app.py:207,232).]

SSTI/reflected XSS via error message in search handler — Code execution via Jinja2 evaluation and reflected XSS using crafted search input that surfaces in the error. [verified: search exception handler formats str(e) (which reflects the injected SQL input) into a template passed to render_template_string, allowing SSTI/reflected XSS (app.py:281).]

XXE via DOCX/lxml parsing of uploads — Server-side file disclosure (e.g. /etc/passwd) and SSRF via external entity resolution in uploaded DOCX XML. [verified: Uploaded DOCX is parsed via Document(file_path) (python-docx/lxml) with no parser hardening or resolve_entities=False, so external entities in crafted DOCX XML are resolved (XXE) (app.py:303).]

Unrestricted file upload to server filesystem — Attacker-controlled files written to disk and parsed, enabling the YAML RCE and XXE chains; no content validation. [verified: Both upload routes save client files to cwd+'/Files/'+fname then parse them (Document / yaml.load) with no content-type, size, or content validation, enabling the XXE/YAML chains (app.py:324).]

Weak unsalted MD5 password hashing — Stolen password hashes are easily cracked, exposing user credentials. [verified: reg_customer hashes passwords with hashlib.md5(password).hexdigest(), unsalted MD5 that is trivially cracked via rainbow tables (app.py:141).]

Missing rate limiting / brute-force protection on auth endpoints — Attackers can brute-force credentials and forged-secret combinations at will. [verified: No throttling, lockout, or rate limiting exists on /login or /register/* routes, allowing unlimited brute-force/credential stuffing (app.py:175).]

Credit card numbers exposed in API responses — Disclosure of full credit card numbers (PCI-sensitive) and PII to any authorized caller. [verified: Both retrieval endpoints place customer_record.ccn into the JSON response as cc_num with no masking, exposing full credit card numbers (app.py:211).]

Verbose SQL error disclosure — Reveals database schema/query internals to attackers, easing injection. [verified: The /search exception handler embeds raw str(e) (SQL/DB error text) into the response, leaking query/schema details that aid injection (app.py:281).]
